fig1a_top_routes_peak_variability: Scheduled (timetable-implied) trip durations of trips starting 07-10h or 17-20h, weekday service. Only routes with at least 10 peak trips are ranked. Variability across trips of one route also reflects different stop patterns, not only timing.
fig1b_top_segments_peak_variability: Segment = (route, direction, from stop, to stop). Scheduled hop times of trips starting 07-10h or 17-20h. Only segments with at least 10 peak trips are ranked. Most segments have zero scheduled variability (identical timetable on every trip).
fig3_distributions_hourly: Top row: 10% seeded random sample of valid hops; all trips. Bottom row: all valid hops; within-segment CV uses segment-hours with at least 5 trips. Early-morning and late-night hours have few trips, so their values are noisy.
fig4_feeder_vs_trunk: Segments with at least 10 peak trips. Feeder = route_short_name starts with 'MF-'; trunk = non-feeder with median trip length at or above the config threshold. This is a heuristic, not an official BMTC label. Speeds use straight-line distance, so they are lower bounds.
fig5_slowdown_and_hotspots: Stop pairs pooled across routes with at least 10 trips in both peak and off-peak. A ratio near 1.0 means the timetable assumes the same hop time at all hours. Hotspot table lists substring matches against stop names; only matched names are analysed.
fig6_completeness_waterfall: Rows after each stage (percentage = share of the previous stage kept). 'scope' = weekday filter (intended); 'structural' = first stop of each trip cannot form a hop; 'quality' = defects. Headline ratio is final analysed hops over raw stop_times rows.
fig7_stop_slowdown_map: Each point is a stop that starts at least one stop pair with 10+ peak and 10+ off-peak trips; colour is the mean scheduled slowdown ratio of those pairs (colour range clipped to the 2nd-98th percentile). No base map. Scheduled proxy, not measured congestion.
fig9_delay_overview: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times (not Bengaluru). 4,606,471 departure events on 'Schedule'-standard trips (4 sampled months of 2024). On time = -1 to +5 min of schedule. Headway panel uses 'Headway'-standard trips: bunched = actual gap under half the scheduled gap.
fig10_delay_routes_and_buildup: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times (not Bengaluru). Routes ranked need at least 100 events. Right: mean delay at the 1st, 2nd... timepoint of a trip (first 15 timepoints); the curve is not monotonic and later timepoints cover far fewer trips.
fig11_actual_vs_scheduled_slowdown: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times (not Bengaluru). Each point is a segment between consecutive timepoints of a route and direction with at least 100 peak and off-peak events (1,442 segments). Points near the dashed line mean the timetable already plans the slowdown that really happens.
fig2_speedup_latency_efficiency: Median of 5 timed runs after 1 discarded warm-up, each core count in its own process. Machine: Apple M3, 8 logical cores (4 performance + 4 efficiency), 16.0 GB. Cleaned rows: 1,999,285. Dataset is small, so Spark overhead limits speedup.
fig8_synthetic_scaleup: SYNTHETIC replication, not real data: cleaned rows copied k times with new trip_id/route_id. One timed run per point; window + aggregation stage only; 8 GB driver heap.
fig12_delay_speedup: Boston MBTA bus, real actual vs scheduled times (not Bengaluru): 8,424,946 cleaned events from months [1, 4, 7, 10]. Median of 3 timed runs after 1 discarded warm-up; each core count in its own process. Real data, not synthetic replication.
